title: Install 3rd Party SSL
text:
## Install 3rd Party SSL
Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000069456

## Installing a Third-Party SSL Certificate
A third-party SSL certificate can be installed through cPanel and then enabled in Brilliant Directories. The certificate provider remains responsible for issuing and renewing the certificate.

## Requirements
To complete installation, you’ll need the issued certificate, its matching private key, and any required certificate-authority bundle. cPanel navigation can change, but the certificate tools remain under SSL/TLS .

## Generate a Certificate Signing Request
Open Developer Hub > cPanel Dashboard .
Open SSL/TLS .
Generate a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) for the live domain and submit it to the certificate provider.
See the cPanel CSR documentation for additional guidance.

## Install the Certificate
After the provider issues the certificate, return to SSL/TLS and open Manage SSL Sites .
Select the correct domain.
Paste the certificate into Certificate (CRT) , the matching key into Private Key (KEY) , and the authority bundle when supplied.
Select Install Certificate .
See the cPanel installation documentation .

## Enable and Verify SSL in Brilliant Directories
Return to Settings > Domain Manager > SSL . Select I already installed a certificate — check for it when offered, then select Check again to refresh the status.

## Renewal
A manually installed certificate must be renewed and reinstalled before it expires. An expired certificate can produce browser security warnings.

## Managed SSL Alternative
Brilliant Directories can issue, install, and maintain a certificate through the Managed SSL Security Add-On .
